 Print Apple is expected to unveil its first touchscreen MacBook Pro at the Pro and tell event on October 28. Apple's Pro and tell event takes place in Los Angeles this Wednesday, October 28, at 10am Pacific time, or 10:30pm IST. The company hasn't confirmed what it will show, but Bloomberg's Mark Gurman expects a busy day of Mac and iPad news. Headlining the list is Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pro. It will be joined by an M6 version of the entry-level MacBook Pro, an M6 iMac and an iPad mini with an OLED display. Marketing chief Greg Joswiak teased the announcements on October 19 with a short "Can't wait to pro and tell next week" post. This is Apple's second event this month. It comes two weeks after the Welcome Home showcase in New York, where the company introduced the HomeView smart display, the HomePod mini 2 and a new Apple TV 4K. The touchscreen MacBook Pro brings OLED and the Dynamic Island to the Mac 
 Writing in his Power On newsletter, Gurman says the higher-end MacBook Pro will come in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes with an OLED touchscreen, a first on both counts for the Mac. The laptop looks similar to current models but weighs less, adds the iPhone's Dynamic Island and runs on M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. It is also expected to cost significantly more than today's top MacBook Pros. Touch will be an extra option, with the keyboard and trackpad staying central. Apple is tweaking macOS Golden Gate so that it presents controls based on whether someone has been tapping the screen or using the trackpad. Tapping a button can bring up a menu around the finger, and the Dock and Menu Bar have been reworked for touch. Gurman has said on his podcast that the laptop could go on sale on November 6. It is quite a reversal for a company whose co-founder Steve Jobs called touchscreen laptops "ergonomically terrible" back in 2010. M6 iMac and OLED iPad mini are expected after a two-year wait 
 The regular 14-inch MacBook Pro will keep its current design but move from the M5 to the M6 chip, which arrived with the Mac mini in August. Reports suggest it could pick up a hole-punch camera, along with a price increase as component shortages ripple across Apple's lineup. Gurman says a redesigned version of this model is planned for next year. The iMac is set to jump straight from the M4 to the M6, nearly two years after its last refresh. Little else is expected to change, though new colour options are possible. The iPad mini, meanwhile, could become the first iPad outside the Pro line to switch to OLED. It is expected to move to the A20 chip from the iPhone 18, and the new screen may push its price up. Apple's Mac lineup will be crowded after Wednesday, stretching from the MacBook Neo and MacBook Air to three kinds of MacBook Pro. Gurman says OLED versions of the MacBook Air and iMac are already in testing, though neither is imminent. A refreshed non-OLED MacBook Air is due early next year.
